# string-singer

A lightweight, secure, runtime-agnostic library for signing and unsigning strings (like cookies) using HMAC-SHA256. Works on Node.js, Deno, Bun, and modern browsers.

## Installation

```bash
npm install string-singer
```

## Usage Examples

### Node.js (Synchronous)
Default entry point. Uses native `node:crypto`.

```typescript
import { sign, unsign } from 'string-singer';

const secret = 'keyboard cat';
const signed = sign('hello', secret);
const unsigned = unsign(signed, secret); // 'hello' (or false if invalid/tampered)
```

### Universal / Browser / Deno / Bun / Edge (Asynchronous)
Uses the native Web Cryptography API.

```typescript
import { sign, unsign } from 'string-singer/browser'; // or 'string-singer/deno', 'string-singer/bun'

const secret = 'keyboard cat';
const signed = await sign('hello', secret);
const unsigned = await unsign(signed, secret); // 'hello' (or false if invalid/tampered)
```

## Migrating from `cookie-signature`

`string-singer` uses URL-safe Base64URL encoding (with `-` and `_`), whereas `cookie-signature` uses standard Base64 (with `+` and `/`).

### Verifying legacy cookie-signature values
To verify signatures generated by `cookie-signature`, map standard Base64 characters to their URL-safe equivalents before calling `unsign`:

```typescript
import { unsign } from 'string-singer';

// Map legacy cookie-signature format to URL-safe format:
// '+' -> '-' and '/' -> '_'
const legacySigned = 'hello.t+D/a...';
const urlSafeSigned = legacySigned.replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_');

const value = unsign(urlSafeSigned, 'secret');
```
